counterfactual_missing_items: No dural tail or hyperostosis is supplied to support meningioma
No midline clival-centered T2-hyperintense mass is supplied to support chordoma
No enhancing mural nodule is supplied to support hemangioblastoma
decisive_items: a 6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale
The lesion involved and expanded Meckel’s cave, with a small extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale
response.rationale: R1 best explains the full distribution: a CPA-centered mass with Meckel cave expansion and trans-foramen ovale extension, which is characteristic of schwannoma. The cystic septated areas and hemorrhagic foci are compatible with a cystic schwannoma. R2 captures the CPA location and cystic architecture but does not explain the foramen ovale/Meckel cave pathway or bone remodeling. R3 and R4 rely on nonspecific bone erosion/calcifications and lack the composite CPA-to-infratemporal distribution.

rejected.why: Only bone remodeling/erosion and calcifications are cited; meningioma would not explain the smooth erosion/Meckel-foramen pathway and lacks dural tail/hyperostosis in the vignette.
Clivus erosion is present, but chordoma would be centered on the clivus and does not explain the CPA-centered Meckel cave/foramen ovale distribution or cystic septa.
Redundant correlated completion of R1; adds a CPA modifier but no independent raw evidence beyond R1.
Redundant correlated completion of R2; provides no additional raw support beyond parent R2.
Redundant correlated completion of R4; it is a narrower subset of the same clivus erosion span.
Redundant correlated completion of R3; it only appends calcifications to the same meningioma reasoning.
